reason: The mucus picture shows a layer released by the colon lining, so putting them together should help protect it.
expectation: The mucus should form a protective layer over the lining.

effect: The mucus-covered lining completes the protection goal while still allowing water to cross.
reaction: The picture makes the mucus barrier's job clear.
reason: The microbes are shown among plant fibres, with fragments becoming smaller molecules, so combining them with the remainder should explore what they make.
expectation: The microbes should turn some of the leftover food into smaller molecules.

effect: The microbes produced small molecules and gas from some of the leftover fibre, completing that goal. The next goal is to connect exchanges with the body.
reaction: It is interesting that some fibre remains even after the microbes act.
reason: The blood vessels lie just beneath the colon lining, so bringing them together should connect the lining to the circulation.
expectation: The lining and nearby blood vessels should form a route for exchange with the body.

effect: The lining first needed the microbe-processed contents; water and small products now cross into its cells.
reaction: I was surprised the blood vessels could not be added yet, but the compatibility hint clarified the next step.
reason: The blood vessels lie beneath the lining and should carry absorbed materials into the circulation.

choice.combine: Colon contents beside a protected lining

expectation: The vessels should connect the colon's absorbed water and small molecules to the blood.

effect: The colon now exchanges water and some microbial products with blood; some products also enter its own cells.
reaction: The different destinations for the microbial products are interesting.
reason: The remaining goal is to connect these exchanges with the body, so the colon and body model are the natural pair.
expectation: The exchanging colon should become part of the connected body model.

effect: The exchanging colon is now connected to the body, completing the final goal.
reaction: The cutaway brings the lining, microbes and blood vessels together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the food remainder from microbes to the lining and blood was most worthwhile: it showed where water and microbial products go.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final connection felt mostly like assembly; it brought the parts together but added little to the explanation of exchange.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the lining could not connect directly to the blood vessels yet. The hint instead joined it to the processed contents first.

arbitrary.text: That prerequisite felt a little arbitrary: the picture showed the vessels beneath the lining, but did not explain why the contents had to be added first.

continue.text: I would probably continue: seeing how microbes and the body interact was interesting, although I would hope future prerequisites are clearer.
